summary: This bill requires the FCC to publish a report within 180 days detailing enforcement of Kari’s Law, including multi-line telephone system manufacturers’ compliance, obstacles to compliance, potential policy improvements, and recommendations for further legislation.

scores.thoughts: The bill requires the FCC to publish a one-time report on enforcement of an existing law. This entails negligible administrative costs with no meaningful expansion or reduction of government spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue collection.

While the underlying Kari's Law addresses emergency 911 calling (which can relate to medical emergencies), this bill only mandates a compliance report and does not engage with healthcare policy, coverage, or delivery systems.
No connection to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions addressing immigration, border security, or pathways to citizenship.
No provisions related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions affecting military or defense spending.
No environmental or climate-related provisions.
No provisions related to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net programs.
No provisions related to schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance regulation.
No provisions related to sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions related to trade, tariffs, or globalization.
The bill has no fiscal impact that would affect deficit spending or debt reduction priorities.
No provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No provisions related to foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions related to voting access, election integrity, or electoral processes.

The bill addresses FCC reporting on multi-line telephone system compliance with 911 requirements. While it involves telecommunications technology, it does not engage with privacy, data protection, or tech regulation policy.
No provisions related to labor rights, unions, or workplace regulations.
No provisions related to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination laws.
